WAC 458-61A-215; RCW 82.45.010(3): REAL ESTATE EXCISE TAX –
EXITING TITLE EXCLUSION. The real estate excise tax does not apply to
quitclaim deeds given for the sole purpose of clearing title if no consideration
passes otherwise. In order for their daughter to obtain a mortgage loan to purchase
a property, daughter’s parents went on title of the property, and intended only to act
as co-signers, not as co-purchasers. Daughter later refinanced the property solely in
her own name, and her parents quitclaimed their interest in the property. Daughter
made all mortgage payments on the property prior to and after the transfer and did
not otherwise give consideration. For these reasons, the quitclaim deed transaction
was not a sale subject to real estate excise tax.
Headnotes are provided as a convenience for the reader and are not in any way a part of the decision
or in any way to be used in construing or interpreting this Determination.
LaMarche, T.R.O. – Husband and wife . . . who shared title with their daughter on a real estate
parcel that was later transferred to their daughter alone, assert that they were on title only to help
their daughter to get a mortgage, and intended to act solely as co-signors. Grantors assert they are
entitled to a clearing or exiting title exemption from Real Estate Excise Tax (REET) on the transfer.
We grant the petition.1
ISSUE
Under RCW 82.45.010(3)(i) and WAC 458-61A-215, are Grantors exempt from REET on their
transfer of real property to their daughter on the grounds that they merely wished to exit title?
1 Identifying details regarding the taxpayer and the assessment have been redacted pursuant to RCW 82.32.410.

Det. No. 23-0196, 45 WTD 059 (May 5, 2026) 60
FINDINGS OF FACT
[In May 2018,] . . . (Grantors) co-signed a mortgage with their daughter, . . . (Grantee) and one of
the conditions of the loan was that they be on title on the underlying real property located in
Washington state . . . (Property). County records indicate that prior to the transfer at issue here,
Grantee and Grantors each held a 50 percent interest in the Property.
On March 9, 2019, Grantors filed a REET Affidavit with . . . County for the transfer of their 50
percent interest in the Property to Grantee, and Grantee refinanced the Property in her own name.
No money or other consideration passed between the parties at the time of sale. Grantors claimed
a clearing or exiting exemption under WAC 458-61A-215(2)(e), indicating that their intention was
to go on title simply as “co-signors” only, not as co-purchasers of the Property, and asserted they
had not made any payments toward the downpayment or previous mortgage.
The Department of Revenue’s REET Program audited the transaction. As part of the audit, the
REET Program requested loan documents and other documents related to the transfer, as well as
Grantee’s bank statements from . . . Credit Union. The REET Program found that Grantee’s mother
was on the bank statements and was on the account as a co-owner, and for this reason concluded
that Grantor had contributed to the payments on the Property prior to the transfer. On this basis the
REET Program denied the exemption, and the Department issued an assessment on December 28,
2022, . . . totaling $ . . . , which consisted of $ . . . in REET, $ . . . in penalties, and $ . . . in interest.
Taxpayers timely filed a petition for administrative review.
After filing the petition, Grantor provided a copy of a document entitled “Account Change Card”
for Grantee’s . . . Credit Union account, which indicated Grantee’s mother was not added to the
bank account until September 15, 2019, approximately six months after the transfer at issue.
Grantor also provided copies of bank statements showing Grantee’s mother was not listed on the
bank statement prior to September 15, 2019, and indicating that the down payment and mortgage
payments were made solely from Grantee’s bank account.
ANALYSIS
REET is imposed on each sale of real property in this state. RCW 82.45.060. The term “sale”
includes “any conveyance, grant, assignment, quitclaim, or transfer of the ownership of or title to
real property . . . for a valuable consideration.” RCW 82.45.010(1). “Consideration” includes the
following:
[M]oney or anything of value, either tangible or intangible, paid or delivered, or
contracted to be paid or delivered, including performance of services, in return for
the transfer of real property. The term includes the amount of any lien, mortgage,
contract indebtedness, or other encumbrance, given to secure the purchase price, or
any part thereof, or remaining unpaid on the property at the time of sale. . . .
WAC 458-61A-102(3); see also RCW 82.45.030(3). Certain exclusions exist from the definition
of “sale,” one of which is the transfer of an interest in real property merely to secure a debt. RCW

Det. No. 23-0196, 45 WTD 059 (May 5, 2026) 61
82.45.010(3)(i). WAC 458-61A-215 (REET Rule 215), the Department’s rule that administers this
statutory provision states:
The real estate excise tax does not apply to quitclaim deeds given for the sole
purpose of clearing title if no consideration passes otherwise. This rule does not
apply to deeds executed for the purpose of adding persons to title, except in cases
of persons added to title for co-signing security purposes only.
REET Rule 215(1) (Emphasis added.)
Grantors claimed the exemption example in REET Rule 215(2)(e) on the REET Affidavit, which
states:
(e) The parents described in (d) of this subsection who have been on title with their
child are now issuing a quitclaim deed to Joseph to exit title. Joseph has now paid
off or refinanced the mortgage in his name only. The parents’ intention was to go
on title as “co-signors” only, not as co-purchasers of the property, and they have
not made any payments toward the repayment of the loan. This transfer is exempt
under this rule.2
Here, the date of the transfer was made on March 9, 2019, and Grantor wife was not put onto
Grantee’s bank account until September 15, 2019, thus there was no commingling or joint
ownership of funds as originally believed. No money from the transaction was given to Grantors
(compare Det. No. 19-0037, 40 WTD 137 (2021)), and there is no evidence in the record that
payments were made by Grantors on the original mortgage. Therefore, no consideration passed
between the parties, and Grantors are entitled to the exemption in WAC 458-61A-215 and RCW
82.45.010(3). Accordingly, we grant the petition.
DECISION AND DISPOSITION
Taxpayer’s petition is granted.
Dated this 31st day of October 2023.
